summary: The candidate fixes the reproduced primary failure by rejecting mismatched, malformed, and corrupt on-disk AOT artifacts instead of accepting them or silently falling back to compilation. It fixes only a subset of the broad schema-robustness issue: schema_version=True is accepted as version 1, and set() leaves a non-CompiledArtifact in the in-memory cache after its validated disk write fails. Request changes for exact metadata-type validation and validation before memory-cache mutation.

tests.what_was_measured: At base acf7e67, a pickle-valid dict was accepted as a cache hit and corrupt bytes were deleted and converted to a compile miss.
Candidate schema regressions and existing argument cache-key behavior; 9 passed.
Related cache-key completeness, compile-hint identity, and candidate schema tests; 35 passed and 2 architecture-dependent tests skipped.
Mismatched keys were rejected, but boolean schema version True was accepted as version 1 and invalid set() input remained an in-memory cache hit despite no disk artifact.

tests.what_was_measured: Both export and run-only load printed PASS against torch.allclose(A + B, C) on AMD Instinct MI355X. The cached CompiledArtifact MLIR contains gpu.binary, rocdl.target, amdgpu, and gfx950.

gpu_execution_evidence: Fresh export and distinct run-only processes both passed on AMD Instinct MI355X with ROCm 7.2.26015-fc0010cf6; raw logs and the 31,838-byte artifact are under /job/review-evidence-j-7c72979d9ca2/.
remaining_limitations: Candidate is Python-only, so no native C++ rebuild was needed. Only the available gfx950 MI355X architecture was tested. Two tests in the related suite were skipped as architecture-dependent. The pickle envelope is inspected only after deserialization and is not safe for untrusted artifacts. Existing pre-schema caches are intentionally incompatible and require regeneration.
